maleWalk:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production 2D pixel-art sprite sheet with TRUE transparent alpha.
Match the approved reference's crisp square pixel clusters, dark one-pixel outlines, limited color ramps (about 3 shades per material), brown-haired adult male, small head, long slim legs, navy/gold long coat, blue scarf, dark fitted trousers, brown boots. This is hand-placed-looking pixel art, NOT a painted illustration or 3D render. No smooth gradients, airbrush, texture noise, antialiasing, tiny filigree or glossy shading.
Every frame is a SINGLE CONNECTED ARMLESS BODY: head, neck, torso, waist, coat, both legs and boots. No arms, hands, shoulder sleeve stubs, weapons or detached pieces. Clean navy torso shoulder attachment area. Face right in the same 3/4 side view. Adult proportion about 7 heads tall; do not enlarge head, thighs or boots. Keep exactly the same face, clothing, body scale and pixel size across every frame.
Create exactly EIGHT WALK-CYCLE FRAMES in a strict 4-COLUMN x 2-ROW atlas. Square canvas, cells taller than wide. Frame order left to right, then next row. Each cell has generous transparent padding, the pelvis centered horizontally, and the same ground baseline. Character about 120 logical pixels tall, displayed with consistent chunky 4x enlarged square pixels. NO labels, grid, shadows, scenery, motion lines or floor.
Natural grounded WALK, not running, hopping, skipping or high knees. Modest stride and very little vertical bob. At least one boot is on the baseline in EVERY frame. The foreground/near leg has a pale horizontal thigh strap; use it to preserve leg identity. The far leg is darker.
Frame 1: CONTACT, NEAR leg extended forward to the right (heel down), FAR leg behind to the left (toe down).
Frame 2: DOWN, near foot remains planted and moves toward hip; far heel lifts behind.
Frame 3: PASS, near leg supports weight almost straight under hip; far knee passes forward slightly, far boot lifted just above ground.
Frame 4: UP, near leg extends behind and rolls onto toe; far leg reaches forward preparing heel contact.
Frame 5: OPPOSITE CONTACT, FAR leg extended forward to the right (heel down), NEAR leg behind to the left (toe down). This is the opposite leg arrangement from frame 1.
Frame 6: DOWN, far foot remains planted and moves toward hip; near heel lifts behind.
Frame 7: PASS, far leg supports weight almost straight under hip; near knee passes forward slightly, near boot lifted just above ground.
Frame 8: UP, far leg extends behind and rolls onto toe; near leg reaches forward to return to frame 1.
Draw real distinct leg poses, not eight copies of one stride. The upper body keeps a stable slight forward lean and consistent shoulder position, scarf and coat move subtly. All boots fully inside their cells.
